title: Find the Kth Smallest Sum of a Matrix With Sorted Rows
summary: Given an m x n matrix where each row is sorted in non-decreasing order, select exactly one element from each row to form an array.
statement: Given an m x n matrix where each row is sorted in non-decreasing order, select exactly one element from each row to form an array. Among all possible arrays formed this way, determine the kth smallest sum.
constraints: Each matrix row is sorted; choose exactly one value from every row.
Return the kth smallest possible sum, counting duplicate combinations.
hints: Start with the single empty sum zero.
Merge one row at a time by forming every current-sum plus row-value pair.
Only the smallest k partial sums can contribute to the final kth result, so discard larger ones each round.
Induction preserves the smallest k sums after each processed row including multiplicities.
editorial: Induction preserves the smallest k sums after each processed row including multiplicities.

tests.explanation: Sorted combination sums are 3,5,5,7,7..., so the fifth is seven.
There are nine combinations and the largest sum is seventeen.
